newsitem.title: USA: Methodist Bishop Cannon, friend of Jimmy Carter, dies.
newsitem.headline: Methodist Bishop Cannon, friend of Jimmy Carter, dies.

text.p: Retired Methodist Bishop William Cannon Jr., a close friend of former President Jimmy Carter, has died at age 81, hospital officials said on Monday.

Cannon died on Sunday morning at Crawford Long Hospital from heart and kidney failure, Dr. James Tumlin of Crawford Long Hospital said. Cannon had been suffering from heart problems for two years, he said.

Cannon was a former chairman of the executive committee of the World Methodist Council and authored 14 books, including "The Book Of Acts," "The Gospel Of John," "The Gospel Of Matthew" and "Jesus The Servant."

He delivered the invocation at President Carter's inauguration on Jan. 20, 1977, and travelled to the Middle East to help with peace talks at the president's request. The men became friends after Carter spoke at a dinner honouring Cannon.
The Cannon Chapel at Emory University was named after Cannon, who was dean of the Candler School of Theology at Emory University from 1953 until 1968, when he was named Bishop.
